name: Variable reward

evidence.basis: Variable-ratio schedules produce the highest, most persistent response rates (Skinner). Neural basis: dopamine reward-prediction-error (Schultz, Dayan & Montague 1997) — unpredictable reward drives the strongest dopamine signal.
evidence.effect_size_note: Robust and mechanistic; magnitude in product contexts depends on reward salience and unpredictability. The effect is strongest when the reward is both variable and meaningful.

pinned_evidence.title: A Neural Substrate of Prediction and Reward
The debate over dopamine's role in reward: the case for incentive salience

mechanism_summary_for_context: Unpredictable rewards drive engagement far more strongly than predictable ones — the brain's dopamine system responds to the *surprise* of reward, not just the reward. A fixed reward ('every 10th action earns X') is weaker than a variable one ('some actions earn a surprise'). This is the engine behind feeds, discovery, streak bonuses, and 'what will I get' moments. It is also the mechanism closest to addictive design — apply with the strongest guardrails in the set.

preconditions.reason: requires a recurring action that can deliver a genuine, variable reward (discovery, result, unlock); not applicable to one-shot flows

applicability.culture_note: The dopamine mechanism is universal; the framing and pacing of surprise (how often, how loud) is an L3 surface parameter

implementations.generation_directive: When the product surfaces results, recommendations, or content, introduce genuine variability in what appears each visit so returning yields discovery, not repetition. The reward (new, relevant content) must be real — variability of junk is frustration, not delight.

Where the product grants rewards (credits, unlocks, bonuses), make a portion variable and occasional rather than fully predictable — an unexpected bonus after a completed action. Never make core value contingent on the variable reward; it augments, it does not gate.

hard_rules.rule: The variable reward must deliver real user value; variability that dispenses junk, empty pulls, or manufactured near-misses is forbidden
No loot-box / paid-random-reward / near-miss / loss-disguised-as-win patterns; no monetary or paid-currency randomized rewards
Do not engineer intermittent reward to maximize time-on-app against the user's interest; core functionality must never require chasing the variable reward
Do not deploy variable-reward intensification toward users showing compulsive-use signals; no escalation of unpredictability to re-hook lapsing users

constraints.boundary_test: Does the surprise add real value the user is glad to receive — or is it engineered to keep them pulling a lever against their own interest?

relations.note: Curiosity gap often co-occurs (not knowing what the reward is), but is a distinct driver: information gap vs reward unpredictability
Variable reward is the reward component that makes habit loops (HA-04) sticky; HA-04 is the full loop, VR-02 is one part

reference_examples.what: Pull-to-refresh delivers a variable set of content — the canonical variable-reward interface; also the canonical cautionary example for the guardrails
Variable, genuinely-valuable discovery on a predictable cadence — variability of real value, not manufactured suspense
Occasional unexpected rewards after lessons augment a habit without gating core learning
